title: DUST STORM ENCOUNTER
description: A dark swirling cloud rises over the ancient trade track. Your caravan is approaching a severe dry dust storm.
historicalNote: Ancient merchant caravans across central India frequently faced intense seasonal dust storms (Andhi), requiring experienced caravan guides to preserve draft animals and cargo.

choices.label: [A] Wait for the storm to pass
choices.resultText: Your caravan halted safely beneath roadside acacia trees until the storm subsided. You lost 1 travel day, but kept all cargo secure.

choices.label: [B] Continue carefully through the storm
choices.resultText: Your caravan pressed onward through the blinding dust. Minor cart repairs and tarp patching cost 15 Mudras, but no days were lost.

choices.label: [C] Take an alternate sheltered bypass
choices.hint: Safe detour • Adds +1 Travel Day • +5 Knowledge
choices.resultText: You guided the caravan through a sheltered valley bypass. The detour took 1 extra day, but you discovered a new regional landmark (+5 Knowledge)!

title: RIVER CROSSING
description: The caravan has reached a swollen river crossing. Strong currents flow between the banks.
historicalNote: Ancient Indian trade routes intersected major river tributaries where local ferrymen (Tarapalas) operated wooden barges for merchant caravans.

choices.label: [A] Pay a local boatman for ferry passage
choices.resultText: The local boatman efficiently ferried your carts and beasts across the deep channel (-10 Mudras). Safe and prompt crossing!

choices.label: [B] Wait for the river water level to recede
choices.resultText: You camped by the riverbank until morning when the waters receded. Travel took 1 extra day.

choices.label: [C] Attempt the crossing yourself
choices.resultText: Your team forded the rocky shallows. You crossed without delay, but wheel repairs at the far bank cost 20 Mudras.

title: ROADBLOCK & TRAVELLERS
description: A group of regional travellers, guards, and toll collectors has blocked the trade highway ahead.
historicalNote: Provincial authorities and guild alliances regulated ancient highways, checking caravan trade permits and collecting standard toll revenues (Shulka).

choices.label: [A] Negotiate using your merchant reputation
choices.resultText: Your respectful greetings and trading credentials impressed the wardens. They granted your caravan immediate free passage (+2 Reputation)!

choices.label: [B] Pay standard highway toll fee
choices.resultText: You paid the standard highway maintenance fee (-15 Mudras) and continued immediately.

choices.label: [C] Wait for the congestion to clear
choices.resultText: You rested your caravan while the crowd dispersed. Travel was delayed by 1 day.

title: BROKEN CART AXLE
description: One of the heavy ox carts has cracked an axle on a rough stone section of the roadway.
historicalNote: Caravan leaders (Sarthavahas) traveled with spare spokes, axes, and timber to repair heavy wooden bullock carts on long overland tracks.

choices.label: [A] Repair the axle with spare timber
choices.resultText: Your caravan team worked diligently to carve a replacement wooden axle. The repair was sturdy, adding 1 travel day.

choices.label: [B] Pay a local village carpenter
choices.resultText: A nearby artisan fashioned a strong hardwood axle quickly (-15 Mudras). Your caravan rolled on without delay!

choices.label: [C] Reorganize cargo tightly across other beasts
choices.resultText: You redistributed the weight expertly across your pack animals, learning efficient cargo distribution (+5 Knowledge, +1 Reputation)!

title: LOCAL TRAVELLING TRADER
description: You meet a travelling regional merchant resting with pack mules: 'Greetings! I have surplus coastal Salt and spices. Would you like to trade?'
historicalNote: Spontaneous trailside barter and trade between passing caravans was a frequent feature of ancient Indian long-distance highways.

choices.label: [A] Buy 1 Salt cargo at a discounted price
choices.hint: Cost: -15 Mudras • Adds +1 Salt to Cargo
choices.resultText: You purchased 1 unit of Salt at a bargain trailside price of 15 Mudras! Cargo loaded successfully.

choices.label: [B] Share market intelligence & regional prices
choices.resultText: You shared news of inland textile prices and learned of coastal harbor demands (+5 Knowledge, +1 Reputation)!

choices.label: [C] Politely decline and continue onward
choices.resultText: You exchanged friendly road blessings with the trader and continued your journey.

title: TRAVELLING SCHOLAR CHALLENGE
description: A scholarly traveler from an ancient learning academy walks alongside your caravan: 'Greetings, merchant! Let us see if you know the geography of our great trade routes.'
historicalNote: Scholars, teachers, and wanderers from ancient centers of learning like Takshashila and Varanasi traveled alongside merchant caravans for mutual protection along imperial trade tracks.
question: Which major ancient highway connected northern Gangetic centers through Ujjain to southern ports?

choices.label: [A] The Dakshinapatha (Great Southern Highway)
choices.resultText: ✓ CORRECT! 'Splendidly answered, merchant! The Dakshinapatha was indeed the lifeblood of inland commerce.' (+10 Knowledge, +2 Reputation)

choices.label: [B] The Trans-Atlantic Route
choices.resultText: ✗ NOT QUITE. 'The correct answer is the Dakshinapatha, which linked Pataliputra and Ujjain to the southern kingdoms.'

choices.label: [C] The Himalayan Glacier Path
choices.resultText: ✗ NOT QUITE. 'The correct answer is the Dakshinapatha, the great southern highway of central India.'
